transcript: So the STT hikes were affected from April 1, 2026 implemented in order to curb the FNO, but a historic shift in India's derivative market has been seen in the month of April 2026. For the first time ever, BSE has overtaken NSE in FNO market share grabbing 55.37% of the total FNO turnover in the month of April against NSE's 44.63%. Now that's a complete reversal from March when NSE held a commanding 56% share. Now look at the numbers. NSE's average daily FNO turnover, it fell nearly 26% while for BSE it was up 20% and the real pain it lies in the options premium. That part actually makes the exchanges money. NSE's premium turnover crashed around 31% while for BSE it barely moved up 1%. But what are the drivers behind this market shift? So BSE charges almost zero on its equity futures and just rupees five per lakh on options while for NSE if you see NSE charges about about 35.53 lakh rupees per FNO transaction that is seven times higher and after increasing the STT by the government from April 1, high volume traders suddenly started caring a lot more about the cost and they moved to BSE. Also in April, BSE had four expiry days, NSE had only three. So that was another advantage for BSE. Lastly, BSE shifted expiries to Thursdays which turned out to be a better trading day than NSE's Tuesday slot and markets have already already reacted. BSE Limited is up 22% in just one month and nearly 70% in a year. Now here it is when it is getting interesting. This shift is happening right before when NSE's of IPOs around the corner. Losing the market share at this moment could actually impact its valuation. So the real question now is that is April just a one-off spike or are we watching a permanent shift in India's trading landscape?
